title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a process of converting categorical data variables so they can be provided to machine learning algorithms to improve predictions. Each category value is converted into a new categorical column and assigned a $$1$$ or $$0$$ $$\frac{true}{false}$$.

title: Effect of Changing Values in One-Hot Encoding
text: When you change the values in a one-hot encoded column, you are essentially changing the scale of that feature. This can affect the coefficients of the linear model but not necessarily the average squared loss.

title: Comparing Models m1 and m2
text: Both models m1 and m2 are trained on the same data, but with different scales for the features. The average squared loss is a measure of how well the model predicts the data. Consider how scaling affects the predictions and the loss.

title: Analyzing the Effect of Scaling on Loss
text: If you scale a feature in a linear model, the coefficients will adjust to compensate for the change in scale. However, the predictions and thus the average squared loss remain the same. Why is this the case?
